newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil kicks off telecommunications sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Brazil kicks off telecommunications sell-off.

text.p: Brazil's plan to privatise its huge telecommunications network effectively began Wednesday as a 20-year cellular phone concession was signed for the region stretching from the Amazon River to the centre of the country.
Several other contracts are in the works.
The Communications Ministry is judging bids from a host of international and Brazilian companies seeking to provide cellular services on the B Band frequency in nine other regions of the country.

Communications Minister Sergio Motta said he expected to open bids next week from companies seeking concessions for the lucrative Sao Paulo area, Brazil's biggest market, and in another area encompassing the states of Bahia and Sergipe.
"I think the proposals will be indecent in their value," Motta told officials gathered at Wednesday's signing ceremony.
Brazil's first cellular contract was to Brazilian-Canadian company Americel, which includes BCE Inc.'s Bell Canada and Telesystem International Wireless Inc.
Officials said they expect to begin service in Brazil's west-central region, which includes the capital Brasilia, by November.

"The reason we're here is because Brazil has great potential. It is seen as the largest market available for competition in the telecommunications market," said Telesystem Vice President Robert Menard.

Americel, which also includes several Brazilian pension funds and U.S. bank Citicorp, was the sole bidder for the B Band concession in the huge but largely uninhabited region stretching from the Amazon to the central state of Goias, where Brasilia is located.
The group paid $330 million for the 20-year concession, well above the government's asking price of $262 million.
Americel officials said they expect to break even on their investment within four or five years.
The company said it plans to undercut subsidiaries of federally owned monopoly Telebras by about 25 percent. Already Telebras has said it will review its rates to compete with the newcomers.
Brazil expects to raise at least $5.0 billion by selling B Band concessions and a further $10 billion is likely to be invested in equipment by the concession-holders.

Other concessions to run paging, satellite and other services are in the pipeline, and the privatisation of the Telebras system itself is slated for next year. Total receipts from Brazil's telecommunications sell-off should reach about $40 billion within three years, officials say.
